newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parlt approves flood relief bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Czech parlt approves flood relief bond issue.

text.p: The Czech parliament on Friday approved a government proposal to issue up to five billion crowns in domestic government bonds to raise emergency funds for flood relief in the eastern part of the country.
According to the proposal, the bonds are intended to be issued to private individuals and institutions and would have denominations ranging from 500 crowns to one million crowns.
The maturity of the issues has not been decided.
The government is also asking parliament to transfer three billion crowns in proceeds from the privatisation of smaller businesses completed earlier this decade for the flood relief effort.
The cabinet on Wednesday approved just over one billion crowns from various sources at its disposal for emergency relief in the floods which began last weekend and have become the worst this century.
The disaster has claimed at least 23 lives according to official reports published by the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Friday, while dozens have been reported missing in the Czech Republic.

The floods, which have also hit parts of neighbouring Poland, Slovakia and Austria, the result of torrential rains earlier this week, have forced tens of thousands out of their homes in villages, towns, and cities.
Damage to buildings, homes, and infrastructure is expected to be in the tens of billions of crowns.
